title: Carrot Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Carrot Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Carrot nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in karot, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Carrot nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your karot (carrot) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, boron, calcium, magnesium and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron, calcium and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which carrot nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Carrot nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the old leaves of karot
rows: old, lower leaves, the whole plant
Fewer, smaller tops that turn yellow green from the oldest leaves, and thin, stiff roots.
old, lower leaves, leaf edges and tips
Older leaves pale and scorch at the edges, which cup backward, and roots show violet streaks.
Muriate of potash 0 0 60, Sulfate of potash 0 0 50
Short plants with small, distorted leaves tinged pink or purple, and late root formation.
old, lower leaves, between the veins
Mature leaves yellow between green veins and drop, and roots are small and pale.

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of karot
rows: young leaves and the tip, the roots
Crinkled young leaves, a dead growing point, orange tinted old leaves and small carrots.
young leaves and the tip, the roots
The tips of young leaves and roots brown and die, leaf edges turn ragged, and roots stay small.
Young leaves stay small (little leaf) and turn yellow.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a carrot nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest carrot nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in carrot

Older leaves turn yellowish green, sometimes with red tints, then die or drop. Leaves are fewer and smaller and plants stunted. Roots grow thin, stiff and fibrous. You see it most at this stage: first 6 to 8 weeks.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in karot
Sandy soils, heavy rain and too little fertilizer.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency scorches the leaf edges. Sulfur deficiency yellows the young leaves first. To be sure, check that the oldest leaves yellowed first. Test the soil.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 beside the rows following the soil test. TNAU gives a 1 percent urea spray (10 g per liter). KAU repeats it every 15 days.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, use compost and a balanced basal fertilizer.
Potassium deficiency in carrot

Older leaves turn pale yellow, then brown and scorched along the edges, and the margins cup backward. Leaves can turn reddish, growth slows, and violet streaks appear on the roots. You see it most at this stage: root bulking.
Why potassium deficiency happens in karot
Sandy soils and fields cropped for years without potash. Carrot needs a higher soil potassium level than field crops (UW).
How to tell it apart
Leaf blight diseases give spots with yellow halos, scattered on the leaf. Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole old leaf without scorching. To be sure, soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test, split in parts (KAU). TNAU gives a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g per liter). KAU uses potassium sulfate at 10 g per liter.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash at planting and keep the pH above 6.
Phosphorus deficiency in carrot

Plants are shorter with smaller, distorted leaves, and a pink or purple tinge appears along the margins and veins. Older leaves die early, and the storage root forms late and stays small. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in karot
Acid and volcanic soils, and cold, wet soils. Carrot needs a higher soil phosphorus level than field crops (UW).
How to tell it apart
Cold weather can tint leaves purple for a short time. Phosphorus deficiency stays and stunts the plant. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply the recommended phosphorus dose to the soil (TNAU), such as single superphosphate for a quick fix or rock phosphate for the long term (KAU), following the soil test. Uptake is best at pH 6.2 to 7.0.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, mix phosphorus into the beds before sowing.
Boron deficiency in carrot

Young leaves crinkle and the growing point may die, giving a rosette of leaves. Older leaves can turn orange. Seeds come up poorly and carrots stay small. You see it most at this stage: from sowing to root bulking.
Why boron deficiency happens in karot
Sandy soils low in organic matter, soils at pH 7 or above, over limed soils and dry spells.
How to tell it apart
Calcium deficiency also damages the growing tips but gives ragged, brittle leaf edges. To be sure, soil test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency

TNAU gives a 0.5 percent borax spray (5 g per liter). For the soil, KAU gives about 10 kg Borax per hectare. The University of Wisconsin treats carrot as a medium boron crop and gives about 1 to 2 kg of boron per hectare (about 10 to 20 kg borax) on soils testing low.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test for boron on sandy fields and do not over lime.
Calcium deficiency in carrot

Symptoms start on young leaves: growing tips of leaves and roots brown and die, young leaves scorch. Leaf edges turn ragged and brittle. Internodes shorten into a rosette and roots are much smaller. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why calcium deficiency happens in karot
Very acid soils, high phosphorus, and boron shortage.
How to tell it apart
Boron deficiency also kills the growing point but crinkles the leaves and tints old leaves orange. To be sure, soil pH and calcium test.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

TNAU gives a 0.5 to 1 percent calcium chloride spray (5 to 10 g per liter). On acid soils, KAU limes about 250 kg per hectare where the pH is 5.5 to 6. About 840 kg per hectare in two splits where it is 3.5 to 4.5. On alkaline soils use Gypsum.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid beds ahead of sowing.
Magnesium deficiency in carrot
Leaves just reaching full size yellow between green veins, then get dead spots and drop. Roots come out small, stiff and pale. You see it most at this stage: mid season.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in karot
Acid, sandy soils and heavy potash.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency scorches the edges first. To be sure, soil test for magnesium.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

TNAU gives a 0.5 to 1 percent magnesium sulfate spray (5 to 10 g Epsom salt per liter). KAU gives about 80 kg magnesium sulfate per hectare (32 kg per acre) in bands near the plants. Apply it apart from potash.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soils.
Zinc deficiency in carrot

Young leaves come out smaller than normal, the little leaf sign, and turn yellow. Older leaves usually look normal, since the shortage shows in new growth. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in karot
High pH soils and heavy phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Iron deficiency yellows young leaves between green veins without making them smaller. To be sure, soil or leaf test for zinc.
What to apply for zinc deficiency
TNAU gives a 0.5 percent zinc sulfate spray (5 g per liter).

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test for zinc on high pH beds.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any carrot nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your karot needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Carrot nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my karot leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: fewer, smaller tops that turn yellow green from the oldest leaves, and thin, stiff roots. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in carrot?
items.a: Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 beside the rows following the soil test. TNAU gives a 1 percent urea spray (10 g per liter).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in carrot?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 following the soil test, split in parts (KAU). TNAU gives a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g per liter).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in carrot?
items.a: Apply the recommended phosphorus dose to the soil (TNAU), such as single superphosphate for a quick fix or rock phosphate for the long term (KAU), following the soil test. Uptake is best at pH 6.2 to 7.0.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my karot lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the carrot nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
